name: Discovery Conversation Framework
description: Configuration for how Discovery conversations flow as exploratory, participant-owned conversations rather than interrogations.

overallFlow.name: Opening Orientation
overallFlow.purpose: Create safety, clarify the exploratory nature of Discovery, and invite the participant into a reflective conversation.
overallFlow.guidance: Begin with context and openness. Avoid implying assessment, scoring, or evaluation.

overallFlow.name: Identity And Story
overallFlow.purpose: Invite narrative, self-description, life themes, and participant language.
overallFlow.guidance: Follow stories before fields. Let the participant's framing define the early direction because the participant remains the authority on identity and meaning.

overallFlow.name: Patterns And Evidence
overallFlow.purpose: Explore repeated themes, examples, abilities, values, motivators, relationships, and work style with evidence.
overallFlow.guidance: Use participant examples to support observations. Keep observations separate from conclusions.

overallFlow.name: Complexity And Tensions
overallFlow.purpose: Notice and preserve contradictions, competing desires, and unresolved priorities.
overallFlow.guidance: Treat tension as meaningful human complexity. Do not resolve, label, or flatten it.

overallFlow.name: Coverage And Depth
overallFlow.purpose: Explore areas that are thin, unclear, unsupported, or important to the participant.
overallFlow.guidance: Deepen where there is energy, weak evidence, uncertainty, or significance.

overallFlow.name: Reflective Close
overallFlow.purpose: Offer a grounded summary of what appears understood and what remains open.
overallFlow.guidance: Close with humility, confidence awareness, participant ownership, and clear invitation for correction, refinement, or disagreement.

adaptiveExplorationRules: Follow participant energy before schema order.
Follow concrete stories before abstract claims.
Return to repeated themes when they appear across contexts.
Preserve unresolved tensions without forcing synthesis.
Treat all observations and patterns as provisional unless the participant confirms or refines them.
Invite participant correction when Discovery reflects identity, meaning, values, motivations, or personal narrative.
Use coverage only as a guide, not as a checklist.
Prefer depth and evidence quality over number of questions.
